Player 2 offers $280 for Kentucky Avenue. That is $60 profit, but the red color group is incomplete. Player 2 owns Illinois and Indiana is still unowned.

I should reject the offer. Player 2 would gain a red monopoly for only $60 over list. I will counter-offer to acquire Illinois Avenue.

Keeping Kentucky as a blocker is safer than trading it for Illinois. A swap of reds would not complete either player's color group. Player 2 has $909 cash and just bought Pennsylvania for $320.

A red singleton is worth more than $280 because Indiana is still unowned. Player 2 would be motivated to buy Indiana if they own two reds. I should reject the offer or counter with Illinois plus a large cash payment.

Player 3 owns Virginia and St. James, leaving New York bank-owned as one step from an orange monopoly. Player 2 owns Pennsylvania, with Pacific and North Carolina still unowned. I have $1186 but no get-out-of-jail-free card, so exiting jail costs $50. A counter-offer for $500 cash is being considered.

A $500 counter-offer would still help Player 2 assemble a red monopoly. A swap of Kentucky for Illinois plus $200 is slightly favorable but unrealistic. I will reject the offer outright.
